newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE encouraged by Belarus compromise deal.
newsitem.headline: OSCE encouraged by Belarus compromise deal.

text.p: Europe's security organisation welcomed on Friday a political deal agreed by the president and parliament of Belarus over a controversial referendum planned for Sunday.

Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti, the outgoing chairman-in-office of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), said he had been encouraged by the agreement reached in Minsk on Thursday.

Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko signed the agreement with Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and parliamentary leaders from both Belarus and Russia, after five hours of talks to defuse a brewing constitutional crisis.

"I am encouraged now that an understanding was reached following a visit to Belarus by Prime Minister Chernomyrdin and that the referendum scheduled for Sunday will not be legally binding," Cotti told a news conference in Vienna.
Cotti was speaking at the end of a three-week review conference at the Vienna-based OSCE ahead of the organisation's summit in Lisbon on December 2 and 3.
The Swiss minister said the OSCE, which has an experienced body of election monitors, would not send observers to the Belarus referendum.
"We decided not to do that," he said. "The reduced importance of the referendum will certainly be a good premise for good dialogue wihtin the country."

A troika of ministers from Hungary, Switzerland and Denmark, representing the past, current and future heads of the OSCE, sent a stiff message to Minsk last week, saying the referendum had no legitimacy because it violated rulings of the constitutional court.

The Minsk talks succeeded in persuading Lukashenko to accept that the referendum on expanding his powers would not be legally binding. In return, the Belarus parliament agreed to drop impeachment proceedings against him.
They also agreed to convene a national congress to debate a new constitution.
